name: Sedongpu Glacier detachment, October 2018, south-eastern Tibet
notes: The order-of-magnitude-class disagreement between published volume figures is recorded in source_volume_m3 (disputed=true) with each figure attributed. Kääb et al. (2021): ice blocked the Yarlung Tsangpo (dam 40–60×10^6 m3) and another mass flow followed on 29 October 2018. dammed_river / secondary_surge are non-nullable booleans in the contract; where the retrieved sources do not state them they are recorded as false, meaning 'not established in the retrieved text', not 'established absent'.

precursors_observed.description: Kääb et al. (2021): surface velocities of Sedongpu Glacier increased from a background of ∼0.3 m/d in 2017 to 1–3 m/d at the end of January 2018, 10 m/d in mid-September 2018 and 25 m/d in mid-October 2018 (offset tracking in repeat Planet, Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data); the glacier advanced by almost 1 km between 19 September and 13 October 2018. No lead time is stated as such.

Kääb et al. (2021): after the 2017 avalanche 'ponds developed on its surface and along the margins'; 'the glacier surface showed several crevassed bulges in January 2018, and progressively more crevasses appeared as the glacier tongue expanded'. No lead time stated.

source_volume_m3.notes: Published figures range from 40–60×10^6 m3 (river dam) through 100 and 130×10^6 m3 (detachment / DEM loss) to lower-bound aggregates of >70 and >150 Mm3 for all 2014–2018 events (Li et al. 2022); they measure different things (detached ice, DEM loss over several events, dam volume, multi-event totals) and cannot be reconciled into a single value, so the range is flagged disputed and carries no best
